description.summary: learn the on-output position of toplevels

protocol.description:
This protocol exposes the per-toplevel position on its output to privileged clients. It is intended for use by accessibility, screen-recording, and remote-desktop tooling that needs to map application-reported coordinates (which on Wayland are toplevel-relative) into compositor-output coordinates (matching the captured framebuffer).
Wayland's standard surface design deliberately hides positions from clients on privacy grounds, so this protocol must be restricted to clients the compositor trusts (e.g. via filesystem permissions on the Wayland socket, or a separate privileged socket).
This is currently a labwc extension; upstreaming as a wlr-staging or freedesktop staging protocol is anticipated.

interface.name: portal_toplevel_positioning_manager_v1
interface.description: The manager creates positioning handles for each existing and future toplevel on the compositor. Bind once per session.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager releases all positioning handles it previously created. Already-bound handles continue to function until their own destroy or until the toplevel is closed.

event.name: toplevel

description.summary: a positioning handle for a toplevel

event.description:
Emitted once per existing toplevel when the manager binds, and once per new toplevel as it appears. On the initial bind, toplevels are emitted in stacking order (back-most first); the client should combine with per-handle `stack_position` events for follow-up changes.
After this event, the compositor emits an initial batch of property events (app_id, title, output, geometry, state, stack_position) followed by a per-handle `done` event marking that initial state is complete for this toplevel.

event.name: popup

description.summary: a positioning handle for an xdg_popup

event.description:
Emitted whenever an xdg_popup is mapped — chromium menus, GTK dropdowns, tooltips, etc. Popups are transient child surfaces of an xdg_toplevel (or of another popup) that render above their parent and frequently extend beyond it. Without per-popup positioning data, agentic clients that sample the captured framebuffer cannot route popup pixels to a single owning entity — the pixels naturally fall under whichever toplevel's geometry contains them, which slices the popup across canvas seams when it crosses a neighboring window's edge.
Each popup emits its own initial property batch (parent, geometry) followed by a per-handle `done`. There is no enumeration on bind — popups are inherently transient and only their CURRENT state matters; they appear via this event and disappear via their handle's `closed`.

event.name: compositor_menu

description.summary: a positioning handle for a compositor-internal menu

event.description:
Emitted whenever the compositor maps an INTERNAL menu — a menu that lives in the compositor's own scene graph and is NOT backed by any wl_surface (so wlr_foreign_toplevel and the xdg-popup protocol cannot see it). Examples on labwc are the root context menu (right-click on desktop) and the per-window menu (right-click on a titlebar).
These render directly into wlr-screencopy output, so an agent client capturing the framebuffer sees their pixels — but without a positioning signal it has no way to route those pixels to an owning canvas. The pixels fall under whichever toplevel's geometry overlaps them, slicing the menu across canvas seams the same way an unrouted xdg_popup would.
Each menu emits its own initial property batch (geometry) followed by a per-handle `done`. There is no enumeration on bind — compositor menus are user-driven and transient; they appear via this event and disappear via their handle's `closed`. Submenus of a compositor menu emit their own independent handles when they open.

event.name: done
event.description:
Emitted after the compositor finishes the initial enumeration (one `toplevel` event per existing toplevel, each followed by their own `done`). Clients should treat the world as fully- described after this event and process all subsequent events as live updates.
Also emitted after each batch of compositor-side state changes affecting multiple handles atomically (e.g. a workspace switch that restacks several toplevels at once). Pairs with per-handle `done` events to give clients clean atomic-update boundaries.

event.name: finished
event.description: Emitted when the compositor has decided to stop offering this protocol (e.g. operator disabled it). The client should treat this as a signal to stop relying on positioning data; existing handles will not emit further events.

interface.name: portal_toplevel_positioning_v1

description.summary: positioning handle for a single toplevel

interface.description:
Carries position+size events for one compositor toplevel. The handle is correlated with `wlr_foreign_toplevel_management_v1` and `ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1` via the `app_id` and `title` events: clients listening to both protocols can match handles by those identifiers.
## Coordinate-space contract
The `geometry` event emits **logical (compositor-layout) coordinates** — i.e. surface-local pixels BEFORE the output's scale and transform are applied. This is the same coordinate system as the rest of Wayland: `wl_pointer.motion`, `xdg_toplevel.configure` size hints, etc.
`wlr-screencopy-unstable-v1` delivers buffers in PHYSICAL pixels (post-scale). On a 2x HiDPI output, a logical 1280x720 toplevel becomes a 2560x1440 region in the screencopy buffer. Clients that want to match positioning data against a screencopy buffer must read `wl_output.scale` (and `wl_output.geometry.transform`) and apply the conversion themselves:
buffer_x = floor(geometry.x * wl_output.scale) buffer_y = floor(geometry.y * wl_output.scale) buffer_w = ceil(geometry.width * wl_output.scale) buffer_h = ceil(geometry.height * wl_output.scale)
Single-output non-HiDPI deployments (the common case) have scale=1, where logical and physical coords coincide and no conversion is needed.
Logical was chosen over physical to keep the protocol consistent with Wayland convention; physical-pixel buffers are an output-specific render concern that clients can derive from the logical position plus output metadata.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops further position events for this toplevel.

event.name: app_id
event.description: Mirrors `wlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.app_id`. Emitted on the same trigger so clients listening to both protocols see consistent state.

event.name: title
event.description: Mirrors `wlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.title`.

event.name: output

description.summary: output this toplevel currently lives on

event.description: The toplevel's primary output. Position events on this handle are in this output's coordinate space. Clients that capture from a different output should ignore this handle's positions.

event.name: geometry

description.summary: current position and size on the output

event.description:
Position and size of the toplevel relative to the most-recent `output` event's origin, in **logical (compositor-layout) pixels** — see this interface's coordinate-space contract for the relationship to `wlr-screencopy` physical buffers.
Emitted on bind for the current state and on every subsequent move/resize that reaches the compositor.

event.name: frame_geometry
event.description:
Position and size of the full compositor-visible toplevel frame relative to the most-recent `output` event's origin, in logical pixels. Unlike `geometry`, this includes compositor-owned server side decorations such as labwc titlebars and borders.
Clients should use `geometry` for app-local coordinate projection (for example AT-SPI rectangles) and `frame_geometry` for matching against captured framebuffer pixels during window movement.

event.name: surface_margin

description.summary: margins between the window rect and the wlr_surface buffer

event.description:
The wlr_surface a CSD client commits is often LARGER than the rect it declares via `xdg_surface.set_window_geometry`. Chromium, Electron, GTK4, and other client-side-decorated apps render a soft drop shadow into the transparent margin between the surface edge and the declared window rect. These shadow pixels are legitimate surface content the compositor draws, but they live OUTSIDE the window's logical bounds.
This event reports those margins, in logical pixels, so that privileged clients matching captured framebuffer regions to a toplevel can include the visible shadow pixels in the attribution rect for that toplevel. Without this signal, shadow pixels get attributed to neighboring toplevels or the desktop background and produce ghost halos as the window moves.
All four values are >= 0. Pure server-side-decoration (SSD) clients (e.g. foot, glfw without CSD) emit zeros — their wlr_surface equals their window rect. Re-emitted whenever the surface buffer size or the client's set_window_geometry changes; in practice that is once on map and rarely thereafter.
Final attribution rect (in compositor logical pixels): x = geometry.x - left y = geometry.y - top w = geometry.width + left + right h = geometry.height + top + bottom

event.name: state
event.description: Mirrors `wlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.state`. Useful for distinguishing the "fullscreen — position is (0,0) by construction" case from "windowed — position is significant." Also exposes the focused/activated bit, which agentic clients use to know which toplevel currently receives keyboard input.

event.name: stack_position
event.description:
Position in the compositor's stacking order, where 0 is the back-most (visually behind everything else) and increasing values move toward the front. Re-emitted whenever the toplevel's z-order changes — typically on focus change, on explicit raise, on a new toplevel appearing above this one, or on this toplevel being closed (in which case `closed` is emitted before any final stack_position).
Critical for agentic use: when two toplevels' geometry events overlap on the same output, the higher stack_position is the one a click at that pixel would actually hit. The compositor guarantees stack_position is unique among currently-mapped toplevels on the same output at any instant.

event.name: content_types
event.description:
Observational summary of wp_content_type_v1 hints set on the toplevel's surface tree. This is a diagnostic signal only: a client hint of video/photo/game does not prove that matching pixels are visible, changing, or worth routing through a video codec.
The mask is a bitset:
1 = photo 2 = video 4 = game
content_type_v1's none value is represented by an empty mask. video_surface_count counts surfaces currently reporting video so the portal agent can distinguish one media candidate from many nested or duplicate hints.

event.name: damage

description.summary: source damage mapped into output coordinates

event.description: Source-surface commit damage for this toplevel, mapped into the same output-relative logical coordinate space as geometry and frame_geometry. This is a candidate-region hint, not a proof of final visible pixels: it is emitted before occlusion clipping and before conversion into wlr-screencopy's physical buffer coordinates. Clients must still validate against screencopy damage or pixel content before skipping unchanged regions.

event.name: done
event.description:
Emitted after a coherent batch of property events (geometry, state, stack_position, etc.) so clients can apply updates atomically. Compositors send this:
- Once after the initial property-event batch following a `toplevel` event from the manager. - After each user-visible state change (e.g. move complete, resize complete, focus change).
Clients should buffer events between this handle's `done` events to avoid observing intermediate inconsistent states.

event.name: closed
event.description: After this event, no further events are emitted. The client should destroy the handle.

interface.name: portal_popup_positioning_v1

description.summary: positioning handle for a single xdg_popup

interface.description:
Carries position+size events for one xdg_popup. The handle is correlated with its owning toplevel via the `parent` event so that the client can route popup pixels to a canvas owned by the same conceptual surface tree, regardless of which sibling toplevels the popup geometrically overlaps with on screen.
Position uses the same coordinate-space contract as `portal_toplevel_positioning_v1.geometry`: logical (compositor- layout) pixels, before output scale. Popup positions are emitted in COMPOSITOR coords, not parent-relative — i.e. ready to be consumed by clients that already operate against screencopy buffers, without a separate parent-position add.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops further events for this popup.

event.name: parent
event.description:
The xdg_toplevel that ultimately owns this popup. For nested popups (a menu opening a submenu), this resolves the chain to the ROOT toplevel rather than the immediate parent popup — clients only need to know which toplevel's canvas tree this popup belongs to.
Emitted once after the manager's `popup` event, before the first `done`.

event.name: geometry

description.summary: current position and size on the output

event.description:
Position and size of the popup in the parent toplevel's output coordinate space, in logical pixels.
Emitted on bind for the current state and on every reposition (e.g. submenu arrow keys, anchor change).

event.name: done
event.description: Emitted after a coherent batch of property events (parent, geometry) so clients can apply updates atomically.

event.name: closed
event.description: After this event, no further events are emitted. The client should destroy the handle.

interface.name: portal_compositor_menu_positioning_v1

description.summary: positioning handle for a compositor-internal menu

interface.description:
Carries position+size events for one compositor-internal menu (root menu, window menu, or any submenu thereof). Unlike xdg_popups, compositor menus have no associated wl_surface — the compositor renders them directly into its scene graph.
Position uses the same coordinate-space contract as `portal_toplevel_positioning_v1.geometry`: logical (compositor- layout) pixels, before output scale. Compositor menus are always stacked above every toplevel and popup; there is no `stack_position` event because their z-order is fixed.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops further events for this menu.

event.name: geometry

description.summary: current position and size on the output

event.description:
Position and size of the menu's bounding rect in the compositor's output coordinate space, in logical pixels.
Emitted on map and on every reposition (e.g. arrow-key navigation that opens a submenu does NOT move this menu but emits a separate handle for the submenu; explicit menu moves are rare but emitted here).

event.name: done
event.description: Emitted after a coherent batch of property events (geometry) so clients can apply updates atomically.

event.name: closed
event.description: After this event, no further events are emitted. The client should destroy the handle.
